problem: Language-conditioned IRL and reward-learning work (LC-RL, AGILE) only uses template-generated NL goals and generalizes poorly to new NL goals and new environments. Goal relabeling like HER cannot be applied directly because NL goals live in a different space than states.
motivation: Humans specify tasks in natural language, so agents should learn policies and rewards that generalize to varied human instructions and unseen environments without a ground-truth reward. On R2R, AIRL with SAC barely beats behavior cloning, because the discriminator (reward) does not generalize to new goals.
key_idea: Learn a variational trajectory-to-instruction goal generator and use it to relabel expert trajectories, relabel policy rollouts as extra positives for the AIRL discriminator, and sample diverse goals for the policy, plus self-supervised fine-tuning in new environments.
insight: Reward (discriminator) generalization is the bottleneck. Ablations show HGR alone hurts (0.427 vs 0.449 base) because generated goals appear only in positives, but combined with EGR it reaches 0.504, and HGS without HGR falls to 0.399. HER on top of AIRL does not help, and HER+HGR collapses to 0.101, since the learned rewards are dense, not sparse. Self-supervised fine-tuning with demos from a goal-agnostic BC policy works much better than random exploration (0.491 vs 0.347 at 15k).
method: Language-conditioned AIRL: discriminator f = g(s,a,G) + γh(s',G) − h(s,G) with attention over goal words; MLP over state embedding, attended goal and action embedding
SAC (modified for discrete actions) optimizes the policy against the learned reward, using a replay buffer
Variational goal generator: LSTM trajectory encoder, latent z (prior/posterior), attention-based LSTM decoder producing NL instructions, trained with ELBO and KL annealing
Expert Goal Relabeling (EGR): generate N=2 extra goals per expert trajectory as additional demonstrations
Hindsight Goal Relabeling (HGR): relabel policy rollouts with generated goals as extra positive examples for the discriminator (0.5 mix)
Hindsight Goal Sampling (HGS): iteratively sample goals from generator-relabeled rollouts (G^v) to train the policy on diverse goals
Self-supervised learning in new environments: a goal-agnostic BC policy πp samples 15k trajectories, the generator labels them as pseudo-expert demos, then fine-tune with the same algorithm (no EGR)

setting.backbone: Seq2seq LSTM base model with ResNet-152 features; SAC policy/Q-network + AIRL discriminator + variational goal generator (trained from scratch, GloVe init)
setting.training_data: R2R train split (61 environments, 14,025 instructions) expert demos; 1M environment interactions; generator-relabeled goals; 15k self-generated demos in unseen environments
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB (36 views, ResNet-152 features) in Matterport3D, state = history of observations encoded by LSTM
setting.action_space: Discrete nav-graph viewpoints (up to 13 neighbors + stop)
setting.privileged: none at test time (no goal position given). Ground-truth reward is not used, but the unseen environments are accessible for self-supervised interaction.

numbers.backbone: AIRL+SAC LSTM seq2seq with variational goal generator
numbers.extra: 1M environment interactions; mean over 8 runs; SR is a fraction

numbers.backbone: AIRL+SAC LSTM seq2seq with variational goal generator
numbers.extra: 1M environment interactions, no self-supervised fine-tuning; SR is a fraction

numbers.backbone: AIRL+SAC LSTM seq2seq with variational goal generator
numbers.extra: further 1M interactions of self-supervised fine-tuning in unseen environments on 15k pseudo-demos from goal-agnostic policy; no expert demos or NL goals in unseen envs; SR is a fraction

numbers_note: Only success rate reported (as a fraction, no SPL/NE); no test-set results because R2R test ground truth is unavailable.
results: LangGoalIRL reaches SR 0.530 on seen validation vs 0.449 for LangGoalIRL BASE, 0.445 for behavior cloning, 0.359 for LC-RL and 0.231 for AGILE. On unseen validation it reaches 0.357 vs BC 0.300, and self-supervised fine-tuning lifts it to 0.491, though the full-supervision upper bound is 0.645.
limitations: Only evaluated on R2R and only success rate; still well below the supervised upper bound (0.645 unseen), and trained with sparse SR-only comparison to non-comparable SOTA
Requires a trained goal generator (BLEU only ~0.32-0.34) and access to unseen environments for self-supervised interaction
HER conflicts with the approach and the strategies have interdependent ablations (HGR alone hurts)
